content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 21.04.2025)
Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on April 18, 2025, the area sown under the Summer crops is 68.80 lakh ha as compared to 59.73 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Of this, area of 31.57 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 27.60 lakh ha (increase of 3.97 lakh ha). 2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 18.04.2025, 79.46% of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 98.00% area of Pulses mainly in Gram (98%), Kulthi (100%), Urdbean (97%), Moongbean (97%); 86.71% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (98.00%); 98.78 % area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (99.30%); 68.00% of Wheat and 52.15% area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25. 3. Rabi Season Area Coverage: For Rabi horticulture crops, major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion – 12.58 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato – 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato – 3.21 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year). 4. Weather Update: a) Temperature: Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over Northwest India & by 4-6°C likely over East India during next 4-5 days and no significant change during subsequent 2-3 days. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01– 21 April, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 15% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -36%; (ii) Northwest India: -29%; (iii) Central India: 10%; and South Peninsula: 76%. An intense Western Disturbance likely to affect Western Himalayan Region from 16th. Thunderstorm accompanied with lightning & Gusty wind speed and isolated Heavy rainfall likely over East and North East India during the Week. A north south trough from central Assam to Tripura and 2nd from central Pakistan & adjoining northwest Rajasthan to central parts of Bangladesh; 3rd trough from northeast Madhya Pradesh to Gulf of Mannar in lower tropospheric levels. Heavy rainfall likely over Arunachal Pradesh & Assam & Meghalaya during 22nd-24th with very heavy rainfall at isolated places over Assam & Meghalaya on 22nd April.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2 5. Inputs Situation: a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 17th April 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 66.82 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 37% of total live storage capacity (182.37 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 115 percent of last year's storage and 117 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Water melon and Musk melon (Fusarium wilt) in Uttar Pradesh. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7.
